relevance_reason: The paper reports a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta who carries compound heterozygous BMP1 variants (the OI13 gene). It also describes functional testing of these variants in zebrafish.

findings.statement: Cho et al. (2015) described a Korean patient with osteogenesis imperfecta who had an umbilical hernia, frequent fractures, markedly short stature, delayed motor development, scoliosis, and dislocation of the radial head with a bowed radius and ulna.
quotes: We applied whole-exome sequencing to identify mutations in a Korean OI patient who had an umbilical hernia, frequent fractures, a markedly short stature, delayed motor development, scoliosis, and dislocation of the radial head, with a bowed radius and ulna.

findings.statement: In a Korean patient with osteogenesis imperfecta, Cho et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing and identified compound heterozygous novel variants in the BMP1 gene. One was a c.808A>G transition resulting in a met270-to-val (M270V) substitution. The other was a c.1297G>T change that caused skipping of exon 10. A zebrafish assay showed that both variants were hypofunctional.
quotes: We identified two novel variants in the BMP1 gene: c.808A>G and c.1297G>T. The former variant caused a missense change p.(Met270Val) and the latter variant caused the skipping of exon 10.
The hypofunctional nature of the two variants was demonstrated in a zebrafish assay.

findings.statement: Cho et al. (2015) tested the BMP1 variants c.808A>G (p.Met270Val) and c.1297G>T (exon 10 skipping) in a zebrafish assay and showed that both were hypofunctional.
quotes: The hypofunctional nature of the two variants was demonstrated in a zebrafish assay.

relevance_reason: Reports BMP1 variants (homozygous 3'UTR polyadenylation-signal variant and a compound heterozygous splice-affecting variant) in children with bone fragility, with functional and bone-tissue studies; this directly characterizes OI type XIII.

findings.statement: Fahiminiya et al. (2015) studied 4 unrelated children with a bone fragility disorder that they had previously described. The disorder was characterized mainly by lower extremity fractures and by a mineralization defect in bone tissue but not at the growth plate level. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography showed elevated volumetric cortical bone mineral density in all 4 individuals.
quotes: a bone fragility disorder in children that was characterized mainly by lower extremity fractures and a mineralization defect in bone tissue but not on the growth plate level
Peripheral quantitative computed tomography showed that all individuals had elevated volumetric cortical bone mineral density.

phenotypes.text: elevated volumetric cortical bone mineral density

findings.statement: In iliac bone samples from the patients, Fahiminiya et al. (2015) found by histomorphometry and quantitative backscattered electron imaging that the onset of mineralization at bone formation sites was delayed, but that the mineralized matrix was hypermineralized.
quotes: Assessment of iliac bone samples by histomorphometry and quantitative backscattered electron imaging indicated that the onset of mineralization at bone formation sites was delayed, but that mineralized matrix was hypermineralized.

phenotypes.text: delayed onset of mineralization at bone formation sites

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing in 4 unrelated individuals, Fahiminiya et al. (2015) found that 3 were homozygous for a variant in BMP1 (c.*241T>C) that affects the polyadenylation signal of the transcript encoding the short isoform, BMP1-1. Skin fibroblasts from these individuals had low levels of BMP1-1 transcript and protein. Less free procollagen type I C-propeptide was present in the fibroblast supernatant than in controls, which indicated impaired C-propeptide cleavage. The authors concluded that isolated lack of BMP1-1 causes bone fragility in children.
quotes: Three individuals were homozygous for a nucleotide change in BMP1, affecting the polyadenylation signal of the transcript that codes for the short isoform of BMP1 (BMP1-1) (c.*241T>C). In skin fibroblasts of these individuals, we found low levels of BMP1-1 transcript and protein.

Both the homozygous 3'UTR variant and the compound heterozygous variants were associated with impaired procollagen type I C-propeptide cleavage, as the amount of free C-propeptide in the supernatant of skin fibroblasts was less than in controls.
These results show that isolated lack of BMP1-1 causes bone fragility in children.

findings.statement: Fahiminiya et al. (2015) found that the fourth individual was compound heterozygous for the BMP1 c.*241T>C polyadenylation-signal variant in BMP1-1 and a BMP1 exon 15 variant (c.2107G>C). The exon 15 variant affected splicing of both BMP1-1 and the long isoform, BMP1-3. Patient skin fibroblasts showed impaired cleavage of the procollagen type I C-propeptide.
quotes: The fourth individual was compound heterozygous for the c.*241T>C variant in BMP1-1 and a variant in BMP1 exon 15 (c.2107G>C) that affected splicing in both BMP1-1 and the long isoform of BMP1 (BMP1-3).

relevance_reason: The paper reports a new OI patient with a homozygous BMP1 mutation and includes functional studies of fibroblasts from two BMP1-mutant patients.

findings.statement: Valencia et al. (2014) described an additional patient with osteogenesis imperfecta who had normal bone density.
quotes: we describe an additional patient with osteogenesis imperfecta with normal bone density and a recurrent, homozygous c.34G>C mutation in BMP1

findings.statement: In a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta and normal bone density, Valencia et al. (2014) identified a recurrent homozygous c.34G>C mutation in the BMP1 gene. Western blot analysis of the patient's dermal fibroblasts showed decreased protein levels of both alternatively spliced BMP1 products and abnormal cleavage of the C-terminal propeptide of type I procollagen.
quotes: we describe an additional patient with osteogenesis imperfecta with normal bone density and a recurrent, homozygous c.34G>C mutation in BMP1

Western blot analysis of dermal fibroblasts from this patient showed decreased protein levels of the two alternatively spliced products of BMP1 and abnormal cleavage of the C-terminal propeptide of type I procollagen.

findings.statement: Valencia et al. (2014) used fluorescence and electron microscopy to show impaired assembly of type I collagen fibrils in the extracellular matrix of cultured fibroblasts from 2 patients: their patient with the homozygous BMP1 c.34G>C mutation and a previously reported patient with a homozygous BMP1 c.747C>G mutation. They concluded that BMP1 is essential for human type I collagen fibrillogenesis.
quotes: fluorescence and electron microscopy showed impaired assembly of type I collagen fibrils in the extracellular matrix of cultured fibroblasts derived from two patients: the patient described here and a previously reported patient with a homozygous BMP1 c.747C>G mutation
We conclude that BMP1 is essential for human type I collagen fibrilogenesis.

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous BMP1 mutation in a consanguineous family with increased bone mineral density and recurrent fractures (OI type XIII), with functional and zebrafish model data.

findings.statement: Asharani et al. (2012) studied a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures.
quotes: in a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures

findings.statement: By whole-exome sequencing combined with filtering for homozygous stretches, Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.34G>C mutation in the BMP1 gene, located in the signal peptide, in a consanguineous family with increased bone mineral density and recurrent fractures. The mutation led to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification.
quotes: Combining whole-exome sequencing and filtering for homozygous stretches of identified variants, we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
The mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide and leads to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification.

findings.statement: Asharani et al. (2012) characterized a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a, demonstrating conservation of BMP1 function in osteogenesis. Genetic, biochemical, and histologic analyses of this mutant and comparison to a second similar locus showed that Bmp1a is critically required for mature collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone.
quotes: We also characterize a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a, demonstrating conservation of BMP1 function in osteogenesis across species.
reveal that Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone.

relevance_reason: Original report identifying a homozygous BMP1 missense mutation in a consanguineous Egyptian family with severe AR-OI (OI type XIII), with functional evidence.

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) described a 15-year-old Egyptian girl (II-3), born to first-cousin parents, with severe autosomal recessive OI. A fracture of the left tibia was noted after birth, and she went on to have 10 to 15 spontaneous fractures per year. Other features were a triangular face, faint blue sclerae, no dentinogenesis imperfecta, normal mental development, a large thorax, and a large umbilical hernia containing abdominal contents. She also had hypotonia, generalized hirsutism, severe bone deformities, arachnodactyly, joint hyperextensibility, kyphoscoliosis, pectus carinatum, platyspondyly, wormian bones, severe short stature (length -11.5 SD), and borderline osteoporosis on DEXA.
quotes: The proband of the family (II-3) is a 15-year-old female, the offspring of first cousin normal Egyptian parents, who was referred to us with history of recurrent fractures and bone deformities.
Since then, fractures occurred frequently and spontaneously with an average number of 10–15 fractures/year affecting both upper and lower limbs.
She had a large umbilical hernia, 5-cm wide and 7-cm long with abdominal content, generalized hypotonia, muscle wasting, and nocturnal enuresis.

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) described the 5-year-old brother (II-6) of the proband. Bilateral femoral bowing was seen on prenatal ultrasound, and both femora were fractured at birth. He had about 15 fractures per year, facial features like his sister's, no dentinogenesis imperfecta, normal mentality, joint hyperextensibility, arachnodactyly, and a large umbilical hernia. Other findings were wormian bones, scoliosis, platyspondyly, and osteoporosis. In both sibs, hearing and cardiovascular examinations were unremarkable, serum calcium and phosphate were normal, and alkaline phosphatase was slightly high. Both were diagnosed with OI Sillence type III.
quotes: Bilateral femoral bowing was detected intrauterine by fetal ultra-sound and fracture of both femora was noted at birth.

Audiological and cardiovascular examinations of both patients were unremarkable. Serum calcium and phosphate were normal, while alkaline phosphatase levels were slightly high. Both patients were diagnosed as OI Sillence type III

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) carried out genome-wide homozygosity mapping in the 2 affected sibs and 2 unaffected sibs. This excluded the known AR-OI loci, and COL1A1/COL1A2 sequencing found no mutations. The analysis identified 2 homozygous regions shared only by the affected sibs: 35.4 Mb on chromosome 3 and 10.27 Mb on chromosome 8p. The 8p region contained BMP1.
quotes: The result of this study showed none of the patients to be homozygous at the CRTAP, PPIB, SERPINH1, SP7, and SERPINF1 loci, while only one of the affected children was homozygous for LEPRE1 and FKBP10, thus indicating further genetic heterogeneity in AR-OI.
The homozygous region on chromosome 3 expanded 35.4 MB around the centromere and contained 151 genes. The 8p region consisted of 10.27 MB and contained 84 genes.

findings.statement: In 2 sibs with OI type III from a consanguineous Egyptian family, Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.747C>G transversion in exon 6 of the BMP1 gene, causing a phe249-to-leu (F249L) substitution. Phe249 lies in the protease domain and is conserved in all astacin metalloproteases. Both unaffected sibs and both parents were heterozygous. The variant was absent from 100 control chromosomes of the same ethnicity and from 884 European control chromosomes.
quotes: found a homozygous c.747C>G nucleotide change in exon 6 that causes the substitution of phenylalanine at position 249 to leucine (p.Phe249Leu)

Segregation analysis of the mutation within the family showed the two affected children to be homozygous for the c.747C>G nucleotide change, while the normal sister (II-2) and brother (II-4) from whom DNA was available and the parents carried the mutation in the heterozygous state.
The mutation was not found in 100 control chromosomes of the same ethnic origin or in 884 normal chromosomes from controls of European ethnicity.

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) studied fibroblasts from the 2 patients. In both, the ratio of pN-alpha-1(I) to pC-alpha-1(I) was reduced and free PICP was decreased, showing diminished procollagen I C-propeptidase activity, although some residual activity remained. A heterozygous sib's fibroblasts showed slight impairment. Collagen was not overmodified, and BMP1/mTLD protein levels were normal.
quotes: Compared to control cells, LF-68 analysis of supernatants from patient-derived cells demonstrated a significant decrease in the amount of pNα1(I) with respect to pCα1(I) in both patients, thus indicating diminished PICP-peptidase activity in homozygous mutant cells

Pepsin-treated procollagens purified from the medium and cell layers of both patient and heterozygous fibroblasts showed a normal migration patterns of collagen type I, III, and V, indicating lack of collagen overmodification

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) overexpressed wildtype and mutant mTLD in NIH3T3 cells and in human primary fibroblasts. Wildtype mTLD caused most pro-alpha-1(I) to be C-terminally processed, whereas the F249L mutant did not increase cleavage. Only the wildtype protein rescued processing in patient fibroblasts. The authors concluded that the mutation strongly reduces BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function.
quotes: In contrast, the supernatants of cells overexpressing mutant mTLD were found with similar levels of proα1(I) C-terminal processing as the control cells transduced with the empty retroviral vector, thus indicating that the Phe249Leu mutation causes strong reduction of the BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function and confirming the pathogenicity of the mutation
found the same result with only expression of the wild-type protein being able to rescue the phenotype of mutant fibroblasts

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) noted that Bmp1-null mice die perinatally and have no gross skeletal abnormalities at birth apart from reduced ossification of some skull bones. However, the mice consistently show herniation of the gut, a feature shared with the large umbilical hernias in the patients.
quotes: Bmp1 homozygous knockout mice are perinatal lethal and although it is unknown whether they could have developed OI later in life, they do not show gross skeletal abnormalities at the time of birth excepting for reduced ossification of some skull bones.
Bmp1−/− mice were reported with consistent herniation of the gut and both the proband and her affected brother have large umbilical hernias with intestinal content.

findings.statement: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) reported that both affected sibs were started on cyclic intravenous bisphosphonate injections.
quotes: Both patients were diagnosed as OI Sillence type III, and cyclic IV biphosphonate injections were started.

relevance_reason: This is the original clinical description of three unrelated children with a new bone fragility disorder that has a mineralization defect. The disorder was later classified as OI type XIII. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Munns et al. (2004) described 3 unrelated children with an apparently novel bone fragility disorder associated with an idiopathic mineralization defect. Recurrent lower limb fractures began with weight bearing. The patients had none of the phenotypic, radiologic, or histomorphometric features classically associated with osteogenesis imperfecta, idiopathic juvenile osteoporosis, or mild autosomal dominant osteopetrosis. The authors concluded that this was a bone fragility disorder of moderate severity that tends to cause lower extremity fractures.
quotes: we describe three unrelated children with an apparently novel bone fragility disorder that is associated with an idiopathic mineralization defect. Recurrent lower limb fractures started with weight bearing.
We conclude that this is a bone fragility disorder of moderate severity that tends to cause fractures in the lower extremities

findings.statement: On radiographs, the patients described by Munns et al. (2004) had increased metaphyseal trabeculation and normal to increased cortical thickness, with no evidence of rickets or osteomalacia. Areal and volumetric bone mineral density of the lumbar spine showed no major change. In 1 patient, peripheral quantitative CT of the radius showed increased cortical thickness and increased total and trabecular volumetric bone mineral density.
quotes: Radiologically, there was increased metaphyseal trabeculation, normal to increased cortical thickness, and no evidence of rickets or osteomalacia.
Areal and volumetric bone mineral density (BMD) of the lumbar spine did not show any major alteration.
Peripheral quantitative computed tomography of the radius showed elevated cortical thickness and total and trabecular volumetric bone mineral density in one patient.

phenotypes.text: increased bone mineral density of the radius

findings.statement: In the patients described by Munns et al. (2004), qualitative histology of iliac bone biopsies showed a paucity of the birefringent pattern of normal lamellar bone. Quantitative histomorphometry showed osteomalacia, with a prolonged mineralization lag time and a decreased mineral apposition rate. The authors concluded that the disorder involves accumulation of osteoid caused by an intrinsic mineralization defect.
quotes: Qualitative histology of iliac bone biopsy specimens showed a paucity of the birefringent pattern of normal lamellar bone.
Quantitative histomorphometric analysis demonstrated osteomalacia with a prolonged mineralization lag time in the presence of a decreased mineral apposition rate.
is associated with the accumulation of osteoid due to an intrinsic mineralization defect

findings.statement: Munns et al. (2004) found no biochemical evidence of abnormal calcium or phosphate metabolism in the 3 patients.
quotes: There was no biochemical evidence of abnormal calcium or phosphate metabolism.

findings.statement: Munns et al. (2004) found no type I collagen mutations in the 3 patients. They stated that the pathogenetic basis of the disorder remained to be elucidated.
quotes: Type I collagen mutation analysis was negative.
The pathogenetic basis for this disorder remains to be elucidated.

relevance_reason: This is the original Sillence clinical and genetic classification of osteogenesis imperfecta into four syndromes. It gives general context for OI classification but has nothing specific to OI type XIII.

findings.statement: In an epidemiologic and genetic study of osteogenesis imperfecta in Victoria, Australia, Sillence et al. (1979) concluded that there were at least four distinct syndromes then called OI. Type I showed autosomal dominant osteoporosis with fractures, distinctly blue sclerae and presenile conductive hearing loss. Type II was perinatal lethal, with broad, crumpled femora and beaded ribs, and was likely autosomal recessive in some or all cases. Type III was progressively deforming, with sclerae that became less blue with age. Type IV was dominant, with variable deformity and normal sclerae.
quotes: An epidemiological and genetical study of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) in Victoria, Australia confirmed that there are at least four distinct syndromes at present called OI.

A second group, who comprised the majority of newborns with neonatal fractures, all died before or soon after birth. These had characteristic broad, crumpled femora and beaded ribs in skeletal x-rays.
The fourth group of patients showed dominant inheritance of osteoporosis leading to fractures, with variable deformity of long bones, but normal sclerae.

findings.statement: Sillence et al. (1979) described a third, progressively deforming group of OI patients, two-thirds of whom had fractures at birth. They had severe progressive deformity of the limbs and spine, and their scleral blueness was less intense than in the first group and decreased with age. All were sporadic cases. The mode of inheritance was not resolved, but the authors considered it likely that the group was heterogeneous, with both dominant and recessive genotypes responsible.
quotes: A third group, two thirds of whom had fractures at birth, showed severe progressive deformity of limbs and spine.

All patients in this group were sporadic cases. The mode of inheritance was not resolved by the study, but it is likely that the group is heterogeneous with both dominant and recessive genotypes responsible for the syndrome.
